title: Cobalt Sentry - Usage & Billing Playback
next_steps: Schedule 1-week benchmark with their test prompts
action_items: Maya: Send pricing + pilot SOW by 2026-08-03
Liam: Prepare mini-benchmark harness and sample script by 2026-08-05

summary: Demo focused on Redwood Console's per-route usage analytics, billing playback and forensic views to support chargeback and FinOps. Heavy discussion on routing fallback, prefix caching, dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs, and security/audit requirements. Customer interested in a short pilot and a benchmark run.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood SE), Jenna Ruiz (Cobalt Sentry Head of ML), Tom Becker (SRE), Rashid Al-Masri (FinOps), Priya Shah (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today, really excited to show you the billing playback and per-route forensic views. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE, with Liam and Sofia from SE. Jenna, do you want to kick off with what you're hoping to see?

[00:18] Jenna: Yeah thanks, Maya. We're trying to get better visibility into per-feature spend. We have three consumer features that all call models differently and our finance team is losing their mind on attribution. So show us how we can slice by route and then, like, play back transactions?

[00:36] Liam: Totally. That's what the console playback is for — you can jump into a route, see every request, token counts, latency, model variant used, and then replay a sequence to see charges broken down. I'll share my screen.

[00:58] [screen share starts, slight audio artifact]

[01:10] Liam: Alright this is the routes page. Up top you get route-level KPIs: tokens, avg latency, cost per 1k tokens, and a lane tag for billing groups. Over here on the right is the list of model variants — if a request fell back from a high tier to a cheaper variant you can see it in the timeline.

[01:38] Tom: Quick question — our teams do a lot of short chat completions and some long-form generation. Can you slice by seq length distribution?

[01:47] Liam: Yep, you can filter on sequence buckets — 0-128, 128-512, 512+. That also ties into the cost estimator since longer sequences tend to keep KV cache alive and change batching profile.

[02:05] Jenna: When you say playback, are you replaying against our models or just showing historical billing?

[02:12] Sofia: Good clar — playback is a forensic view of historical requests; it doesn't re-run models in prod. It will reconstruct the token accounting and show you what was charged and which routing decision was made. For active load testing we can run a separate benchmark harness, which Liam can set up.

[02:35] Rashid: We need this for chargeback to product teams. Can you attach tags that map to our internal cost centers?

[02:43] Liam: Absolutely. Routes already support arbitrary tags and you can map them to chargeback codes. The console supports export to CSV and direct integration with our billing API so you can pull a per-route ledger.

[03:02] Priya: Security question — audit logs and retention. We're regulated so we need immutable logs and SSO.

[03:10] Sofia: We support SAML/SSO and RBAC at the route level. Audit logs are stored for X days by default and we have an enterprise option for longer retention and write-once logs to your S3 (or on-prem) via our Private deployment. We'll share the SOC2 whitepaper after.

[03:35] Maya: Quick demo of a playback — I'm clicking into the "checkout-price" route. You can see a timeline of requests. If I pick a single request — timestamp, prompt tokens, completion tokens, model used, and cost.

[03:55] [clicks, short pause] Speaker 1: (inaudible) oh that's neat

[04:05] Liam: Also note the "why rerouted" annotation — here a request hit capacity on our preferred pool, so our smart routing fell back to a compatible quantized variant to avoid increased latency. The cost column shows the delta so you can trace the cost impact of fallbacks.

[04:28] Jenna: How often do those fallbacks happen? We saw a few spikes when we shipped the new ranking model.

[04:36] Liam: You can surface fallback rates per route and alert on percent of requests that used fallback over a time window. We also have a heatmap of fallback per region so you can correlate with infra incidents.

[04:52] Rashid: For billing we need an auditable trail per user ID — is PII included in these exports? We can't have user ident in the console for compliance.

[05:02] Sofia: By default exports are pseudonymized and we redact PII. If you need a specific schema we can configure a de-id pipeline or deliver logs to your secure bucket so you keep the raw but controlled logs.

[05:18] Tom: Can you show an example of the cost decomposition? Like how much of the cost is model compute vs routing premium vs token pricing?

[05:27] Liam: Yep — here's the cost breakdown widget. Token cost, model variant multiplier, routing premium (for reserved pools), and optional add-ons like longer KV retention. In this example the kickoff feature had high completion tokens which drove most of the spend.

[05:46] Jenna: Does it account for batching savings? We batch server-side sometimes and get token-level discounts.

[05:53] Liam: We do. The billing engine is aware of effective batching; we show a metric called "effective tokens per compute unit". If your batching increases, effective cost per token drops and you can see that historic delta per route.

[06:10] Rashid: Any way to do predictive forecasting? We want to forecast next quarter spend based on current ramp and promo pushes.

[06:17] Maya: There's a forecasting tab where you set growth assumptions or import your usage driver (monthly active users, api calls), and it runs scenario analysis. It's not ML forecasting of demand but simple parametric scenarios with sensitivity bands.

[06:32] Priya: Back to security: encryption at rest and KMS. How are customer keys handled for Private?

[06:39] Sofia: Private supports BYOK via KMS/HSM. You control keys, and audit logs show key usage. For hosted we use envelope encryption and can provide key access agreements for enterprise.

[06:54] Tom: Okay show me a deeper example — like reconstructing a 1-hour window where cost spiked.

[07:00] Liam: Sure — switching to the anomalies pane. You can jump to a spike and press "open forensic range" which populates every request in that range. Here we can group by user-agent, route, model variant, and token buckets. I'm grouping by route.

[07:22] [pause]

[07:26] Jenna: That will be super useful. Can you export that range into our ledger format?

[07:31] Liam: Export CSV or push to your S3 or to our billing API. The CSV schema includes timestamps, route, tag, cost breakdown, and pseudonymized identifiers if you want.

[07:45] Rashid: For our chargeback, we need daily aggregates per product team and a week-by-week diff. Can console do scheduled exports?

[07:54] Maya: You can schedule reports and also create a dashboard that posts to a webhook. Many customers push daily aggregates to their internal FinOps system.

[08:08] Tom: About dedicated capacity — how do cost and latency tradeoffs look? We have a use case for lower SLOs on certain internal routes.

[08:17] Liam: Dedicated (reserved) gives you predictable throughput and lower unit price at the expense of commit. The console helps you simulate committed vs on-demand by modeling expected utilization and showing blended unit price. For internal low-latency routes you can pin them to a dedicated pool.

[08:33] Jenna: How does routing pinning work? We want certain traffic always served from dedicated, others auto-fallback to hosted.

[08:40] Sofia: You define route policies. Policy examples: pin to pool A, fallback to pool B on errors, or prefer low-cost variant and only use high-end variant when SLO breaches. Policies are evaluated in order.

[08:56] Rashid: We're concerned about cost anomalies — can you alert on sudden per-route cost changes and automatically throttle?

[09:04] Liam: Yes alerts on absolute and relative cost deltas. For auto-mitigation we have a guardrail feature that can throttle or route to cheaper variants when a budget threshold is hit.

[09:17] Jenna: Can we map this to a Slack channel for product owners?

[09:20] Maya: Integrations include Slack, PagerDuty, and email. You can map alerts to channels and include a link to the forensic playback for fast triage.

[09:35] [transition to a specific demo of a playback item]

[09:40] Liam: I'm opening a specific request — you can see the prompt, scrubbed completions, tokens counted, and a little note that says "KV cache hit rate 0.82". That explains why latency stayed low for this burst.

[10:00] Priya: That KV cache note — what data does it expose? We only want operational metadata not content.

[10:07] Sofia: Only operational metadata, TTLs, and cache hit/miss stats — content is not shown unless you opt in for debugging with strict controls.

[10:20] Rashid: On the pilot — how would you recommend we run a 1-week pilot to validate cost numbers?

[10:27] Maya: Short plan: 1) pick 2 representative routes (one chat, one long-gen), 2) run parallel traffic for a day against our hosted with sample prompts and your variant weights, 3) run a 1-week production shadow where you route a small percent through Redwood and compare. Liam can orchestrate the harness.

[10:46] Liam: I'll prepare a harness that records identical calls and we'll produce a side-by-side ledger. We recommend including peak-hour ramp tests.

[10:55] Jenna: Any limitations on prompt sizes or token counts in hosted?

[11:00] Sofia: Hosted supports up to 32k sequences on some variants, smaller on others; we'll include the model limits table in the doc pack.

[11:12] [15-minute skip captured as brief side conversation about scheduling]

[26:30] Maya: Back to console — I want to show the rate card mapping. This is where you can see modeled unit prices per variant and apply your reserved discounts. You can change the commit assumptions and watch the blended rate update.

[26:51] Rashid: Can we put a cap per route so teams don't overspend?

[26:56] Liam: Yes route-level budgets and soft/hard limits. Soft limits trigger alerts, hard limits can block requests or route to cheaper variants.

[27:10] Tom: For compliance we need a copy of the architecture diagram showing network egress flows for private deployment.

[27:18] Sofia: Noted. I'll attach the Private deployment network diagram in the follow-up.

[27:27] Jenna: Anything we should be wary of switching from our current provider? Performance regressions?

[27:35] Liam: We try to make model variants Redwood-verified but there can be small differences across model families. Our Optimize suggestions will propose quantization or different variants with estimated quality delta. We also provide eval hooks so you can run your prompts and compare scores automatically.

[27:55] Rashid: Pricing ask — we need a blended estimate across 3 scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive.

[28:02] Maya: We'll produce a 3-scenario pricing and a pilot SOW.

[28:10] Priya: Will you share SOC2 and pen-test results?

[28:14] Maya: Yes, SOC2 and our recent pen test summary will be in the package.

[28:21] Jenna: Okay last thing — can you show how product owners will actually use the UI day-to-day?

[28:28] Liam: Sure — demo quickboards: pick a route, pin the token trend widget, set alerts, and then use the playback link to open any event. It's designed for a product owner rather than an infra engineer.

[28:45] [brief pause — background chatter]

[28:52] Maya: Alright we're running close to time— quick recap and next steps.

[28:57] Maya: Recap: showed per-route KPIs, billing playback, cost decomposition, fallback analytics, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and security options. Action items and docs to share.

[29:12] Jenna: That was really helpful. We'd like to move to a 1-week pilot with two routes and run the benchmark harness.

[29:20] Rashid: I'll circulate internal stakeholders and confirm budget.

[29:25] Tom: I'll work with Liam on the infra details for the shadow tests.

[29:30] Maya: Great — final next steps: Maya will send pricing and SOW, Liam and Sofia will send the harness and private network diagram and we'll schedule the pilot start for the week of 2026-08-10 pending sign-off.

[29:44] Jenna: Perfect. Thanks everyone.

[29:48] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the doc pack.

[29:52] [meeting ends, screen share stops]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words around 03:55 and 11:12, some speaker attribution used generic labels in the screen share section.

End of transcript.
